title: OpenAI publishes an AI-generated, Lean-checked answer to the Navier–Stokes problem
friendlyTitle: OpenAI shared a computer-checked attempt at a famous unsolved maths problem
summary: OpenAI says an internal model and roughly 10,000 coordinating agents produced a proposed resolution of the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness Millennium Prize problem, followed by a Lean formalization using GPT-6 Astra. The paper and proof code are public, but the extraordinary mathematical claim still requires independent expert scrutiny and formal recognition is not automatic.
friendlySummary: OpenAI says thousands of AI agents created a proof and converted it into Lean code that checks each logical step. The files are public, but independent mathematicians still need to examine the claim carefully.
whyItMatters: A machine-checkable artifact gives researchers more to inspect than a confident model answer, while also showing the scale now being applied to scientific problems: OpenAI reports about 130 billion output tokens for the Navier–Stokes effort. The practical standard should remain reproducibility and independent review, not the size of the agent swarm or the announcement.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI research is easier to trust when experts can inspect the evidence and computers can check the logic. A major announcement is not the same as independent confirmation.
